summary: Same swirl-of-arcs geometry and an exactly matching arm-count dial law, but the port renders ~3x dimmer with a hot-core/black-rim radial falloff the original does not have, its ColorSpeed dial runs in the opposite direction, its disc never re-fills after the first ~10 s, and its spatial detail is hard-capped at 16x16.
observations: Rig: 16x16 grid, 256 px, both sides compile and run clean (no compile/runtime errors, wantsSensors false on both, seed-independent — seeds 1/7/1234 give byte-identical frames on both sides).

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: the original's first slider is named `sliderNumArcs` (label NumArcs); the port names it `sliderNumberOfArms` (label NumberOfArms). The other three (`sliderColorSpeed`, `sliderAnimateSwirl`, `sliderSwirlSpeed`) match in name and kind. All four probe responsive on both sides (orig maxDeltaLit 46.9/4.1/13.0/11.5; port 30.1/9.5/6.1/7.1).

BRIGHTNESS: over a 240 s / 5 fps survey the original averages meanBrightness 35 (range 3..59, visibly breathing) while the port averages 12.4 (range 2..16, nearly flat). The gap survives dialing: at NumArcs/NumberOfArms = 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 the means are orig 11/26/40/48/54 vs port 5/12/21/25/31 — a consistent ~2x deficit at matched dials, ~3x untouched.

RADIAL FALLOFF is the root of the brightness gap, and it is not global dimming: at NumArcs=1, t=3 s, the per-radius mean value runs orig 135,139,144,226,185,193,216,174 for r=1..8 (flat-to-rising, peaking mid-radius and at the rim) versus port 225,235,196,102,66,63,58,31 (monotone ~7x decay from centre to rim). The port's CORE is brighter than the original's while its rim is nearly black, so the original reads as an evenly-lit glowing disc/donut and the port as a hot centre with thin fading arms. Same result untouched (t=0.6/3/5.95 s) and at NumArcs=0.5.

BREATHING CYCLE differs. Tracking the occupied radius band (per-radius mean > 8) every 2 s over 120 s at 20 fps: the original expands to the full disc (r=1..8) at t=2-8 s, contracts to a thin r=4-5 ring by t=26 s, re-expands, contracts again ~t=44 s, then re-fills the WHOLE disc again at t=62-74 s — an ~18 s sub-cycle riding a ~62 s super-cycle. The port fills the disc only once (t=2-6 s), then contracts monotonically to r=4-4 by t=56-60 s and thereafter only ever re-expands to r=2-6 (t=80-86 s) before collapsing again at t=104-110 s — a single ~48 s cycle with no full re-fill and no 18 s sub-cycle.

That divergence is plainly visible mid-run: at t=65-75 s the original is a dense, bright, disc-filling rainbow pinwheel (radii 1..8 all 100% lit) while the port is a thin rainbow annulus occupying only radii 3-5 with a black core and black rim. At t=170-180 s the original is a clean solid-RED donut (hue spread ~0 across every lit pixel) while the port is a full-spectrum 5-arm pinwheel.

COLOR: both sides walk hue slowly and both alternate between near-monochrome and full-rainbow phases, so the palette FAMILY matches. Untouched, however, the port's hue advances ~2.4x faster than the original's (survey aggregate hue: orig ~1.6 deg/s, port ~3.8 deg/s), which is why the two are almost never at the same colour phase.

ARM COUNT matches exactly. Dominant angular harmonic in the r=4..6.5 annulus at t=3 s across the arc dial: NumArcs 0->k=4, 0.1->3, 0.15->4, 0.25->5, 0.35->6, 0.4->7 — identical on BOTH sides, including the non-monotone 4->3->4 kink at 0/0.1/0.15. At NumArcs=0 both sides draw the same 'figure-8' twin-loop outline. The geometry function is clearly right.
UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS differ: the original's untouched dominant harmonic is k=8 (~8 arcs, roughly NumArcs 0.6), the port's is k=5 (~5 arms, roughly 0.25). Both are stable across t=0.6/3/5.95 s.

RESOLUTION SCALING diverges. Re-rendered at 8x8 / 32x32 / 48x48 / 64x64, the port's frame is exactly block-constant at 2x2 / 3x3 / 4x4 (256/256 constant 4x4 blocks at 64x64) and its lit fraction is pinned at 41.8% for every grid >= 16 — its spatial detail is capped at 16x16. The original rasterizes at native resolution: lit fraction 93.8% -> 28.9% -> 15.8% -> 9.9% across 8/32/48/64, resolving into fine dotted spiral arcs at 64x64. Invisible on the default 16x16 rig, but a real fidelity gap on any larger matrix.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING: both sides are frame-coupled (the t=3 s frame differs at 10/20/40 fps on both), so this is not a port-only bug. Magnitudes differ though — the port's mean lit value at t=3 s falls 89 -> 74 -> 46 across 10/20/40 fps while the original's stays 199 -> 189 -> 144, i.e. the port loses brightness faster as frames get denser.

STEADY STATE: neither side dies. At --skip 200 --seconds 20 --fps 20 both are alive with zeroMotionFrames 0 (orig mean 39.5, port mean 13.0); the port's dimness and ring-collapse are its steady state, not a decay.

dials.name: NumArcs (orig) / NumberOfArms (port)
dials.origEffect: Sets the number of spiral arcs; angular harmonic k goes 4,3,4,5,6,7 for values 0,0.1,0.15,0.25,0.35,0.4 and keeps climbing past resolvable k above 0.5. Mean brightness rises 11->54 across 0..1 as the disc fills in.
dials.portEffect: Identical arm-count law — same k sequence 4,3,4,5,6,7 at the same values, same figure-8 shape at 0, same dense filled disc at 1. Mean brightness rises 5->31 across 0..1, i.e. the same monotone direction at roughly half the original's level.

dials.name: sliderColorSpeed
dials.origEffect: REVERSED sense: 0 is the fastest hue walk (~2.1 deg/s, spatial hue spread growing 7->33 deg over 25 s) and 1 freezes colour completely (hue moves 0->4 deg in 25 s, spatial spread ~0 — the whole 30 s render is pure red). Rate by value: 0->2.1, 0.25->0.48, 0.5->0.28, 0.75->0.20, 1->0.16 deg/s.
dials.portEffect: Opposite direction: 0 is the SLOWEST (~1.0 deg/s, half the original's fast end) and the rate climbs steeply — 0.25 reaches 123 deg of hue by t=25 s, and at 0.5/0.75/1 the disc is a fast-churning full spatial rainbow (spread 40-90 deg) cycling the wheel several times in 30 s. No port setting reproduces the original's frozen-hue end; no original setting reproduces the port's fast rainbow.

dials.name: sliderAnimateSwirl
dials.origEffect: Binary toggle (0 vs 0.5 vs 1 give exactly the same |0-x| pixel diff, so 0.5 and 1 are the same state). At 0 the disc develops into a ring with one bright swirl arm; at 1 it stays a denser, more uniform mesh disc. Diff |0 vs 1| grows 7.4 -> 48.3 mean-abs over t=2..11 s (~1.05x the side's own mean).
dials.portEffect: Also a binary toggle with the same 0.5==1 identity, and the same relative magnitude of change (diff 2.0 -> 26.3 over t=2..11 s, ~1.10x its own mean). The two port states look more alike in gross structure than the original's two do, but direction and character agree.

dials.name: sliderSwirlSpeed
dials.origEffect: Continuous knob, monotone: |0 vs 0.5| diff 0.3/5.1/6.6/11.1 at t=2/5/8/11 s, |0 vs 1| diff 5.4/17.7/37.1/43.2 — divergence accumulates with time, as a rate control should. Does not produce rigid rotation (angular cross-correlation of the disc profile shows 0 deg/0.2 s shift at every SwirlSpeed); it winds/unwinds the spiral rather than spinning it.
dials.portEffect: Same character: continuous, monotone, time-accumulating (|0 vs 0.5| 0.7/3.7/9.1/12.4; |0 vs 1| 5.8/14.3/16.1/29.7), and likewise no rigid rotation.

feedback: Rename the port's first slider from `sliderNumberOfArms` back to the original's `sliderNumArcs` (label 'NumArcs') — the arm-count behaviour behind it is already exactly right, only the exposed control name differs.

Fix the radial brightness profile — this is the biggest visible gap. At matched dials (NumArcs=1, t=3 s) the original's per-radius mean value is roughly flat-to-rising from centre to rim (135,139,144,226,185,193,216,174 for r=1..8) while the port decays ~7x outward (225,235,196,102,66,63,58,31). The port is over-bright at the core and far too dark from r>=4 out. Removing that centre-weighted falloff should also close the ~2-3x whole-rig mean-brightness deficit (orig 35 vs port 12.4 over 240 s) on its own.

Reverse the ColorSpeed mapping. On the original, ColorSpeed=0 gives the FASTEST hue walk (~2.1 deg/s) and ColorSpeed=1 freezes hue entirely (pure red, zero spatial hue spread, for 30 s straight); the port does the opposite (0 = ~1.0 deg/s, 1 = a full spatial rainbow cycling the wheel several times in 30 s). Also rescale: the port's slow end is still ~6x faster than the original's slow end, and the original's whole range spans only 0.16..2.1 deg/s.

Untouched (no controls set), the port draws ~5 arms where the original draws ~8 (dominant angular harmonic k=5 vs k=8, stable across t=0.6/3/5.95 s). Since the dialed arm-count law already matches exactly, this is just a wrong initial value for the arc-count global — set it to whatever NumArcs~0.6 produces.

Untouched hue speed is ~2.4x too fast on the port (~3.8 deg/s vs the original's ~1.6 deg/s), i.e. the initial ColorSpeed global is also set wrong; fixing the reversed mapping above may or may not cover this, so check the untouched render separately.

Restore the radius 'breathing'. The original expands to fill the whole disc (occupied radii 1..8) about every 62 s — at t=2-8 s and again at t=62-74 s — with an ~18 s contraction/expansion sub-cycle in between (thin r=4-5 ring at t=26 s and t=44 s). The port fills the disc only once at the start, then contracts to a single r=4 ring by t=56 s and never re-expands past r=2-6, on a single ~48 s cycle with no sub-cycle. Watch it side by side at t=65-75 s: the original is a disc-filling pinwheel, the port a thin annulus with a black core.

Lift the 16x16 spatial-resolution cap. Rendered on a 64x64 grid the port's output is exactly 4x4-block constant (256/256 blocks) and its lit fraction is pinned at 41.8% for every grid size >= 16, while the original rasterizes at native resolution (lit fraction 93.8/28.9/15.8/9.9% at 8/32/48/64, resolving into fine dotted arcs). Something in the port quantizes pixel coordinates to a fixed 16 steps instead of using the rig's real resolution. Not visible on the default 16x16 rig, but wrong on any larger matrix.
